newsitem.title: UK: Sugar freight orders slacken, origins mixed.
newsitem.headline: Sugar freight orders slacken, origins mixed.

text.p: Business was quiet at the end of the week on the sugar freight market with only a handful of orders cited from mixed origins, shipbrokers said on Friday.
"In terms of what it should be at this time of year, it's very quiet although it seems to have picked up today," said one.
Czarnikow-Rionda issued a new order for 12/14,000 tonnes of bagged sugar from Antwerp/Hamburg to Aqaba for prompt/onwards shipment.

Lorico, which sold Syria's General Foreign Trade Organisation for Chemicals and Foodstuffs (GEZA) 13,000 tonnes of raw sugar in a tender this week, quoted for 13,000 tonnes in bulk from Cuba to Syria for January 5/15.
Mauritius Sugar Syndicate was in the market for 14,250/14,500 tonnes of bulk sugar on its usual Port Louis to London run for 19/23 December.
Cargill was also active at the end of the week, amending one previous order and issuing a new one.

Cargill cited any December dates for its 14,000-tonne bulk order from Veracruz to Morocco/Black Sea/Egyptian Med/Baltic and also quoted for a same-sized cargo from Maceio or Recife to the same options for 7/15 December.
